lead.title: News live: parents of Australian surfers killed in Mexico fly in for trial; Labor pressured to toughen lobbying rules
lead.summary: Follow the day’s news live The independent member for Curtin, Kate Chaney , will put forward a bill to establish Australia’s first legislated mandatory framework for the use of automated decision-making in government this week. The use of the controversial tool within the aged care sector has affected hundreds of applications for out-of-home care. It’s not clear if there’s a human who can actually apply a common sense overlay to these decisions. And it’s not clear how you can review these if they’re made by a computer. So the bill that I’m introducing today would actually create a mandatory framework that applies whenever government is using an automated system to make a decision that affects people’s significant rights and would require those three things to be addressed: transparency, human oversight, and review. They are driving users – often young people – down rabbit holes of harmful content. We also know harmful algorithms can be devastating for young people and body-image issues. Continue reading...

Science.title: Scientists find a weak spot in one of the deadliest brain cancers

The strategy works by restoring activity of PP2A, an enzyme that glioblastoma cells appear to suppress. Human testing will be needed to determine whether the approach is safe and effective.
